body.objective: Students will be able to contrast preterite and imperfect.
body.iCan: I can contrast preterite and imperfect.
successCriteria: I can tell the difference between the preterite and the imperfect
I can use both tenses to narrate a past trip
I can explain why each tense is used
body.hook: Tell a story about a trip and you'll naturally switch between two kinds of past: the background ("It was sunny, we were tired") and the events ("We arrived, I lost my passport"). Spanish uses two different tenses for these: the imperfect and the preterite.

vocabulary.definition: The preterite: completed actions at a specific time.
The imperfect: descriptions, background, habits and ongoing actions in the past.
Always / every day (often with the imperfect).

study.title: Contar un viaje
study.question: How do I tell a story about the past in Spanish?
study.passage:
Preterite (completed events):
• -ar: viajé, viajaste, viajó, viajamos, viajasteis, viajaron
• -er/-ir: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron
• Irregular: ir/ser → fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron; tener → tuve; hacer → hice
Imperfect (background and habits):
• -ar: viajaba, viajabas, viajaba, viajábamos, viajabais, viajaban
• -er/-ir: comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían
• Irregular: ser → era; ir → iba; ver → veía
Use the imperfect for: weather, time, age, feelings, descriptions, repeated actions, what was happening.
Use the preterite for: actions that started and ended, a sequence of events, something that interrupted.
Story:
"El verano pasado, mi familia y yo fuimos a México. Hacía mucho calor y el cielo estaba azul. Todos los días, íbamos a la playa y comíamos tacos de pescado. Un día, mientras nadaba en el mar, de repente vi un delfín. ¡Fue increíble! Después, visitamos las pirámides de Teotihuacán. Mi hermana estaba cansada, pero yo estaba muy contento. Volvimos a Calgary el 15 de agosto."
English support: Hacía mucho calor = it was very hot; mientras nadaba = while I was swimming; un delfín = a dolphin; Volvimos = we returned.
Activity: Highlight preterite verbs in one colour and imperfect verbs in another, then tell a partner about a real or imagined trip.
study.source: Original story written for this lesson.
steps: Learn when to use each tense
Tell a partner about a trip
discussion: Why is "Hacía mucho calor" in the imperfect?
Why is "vi un delfín" in the preterite?
What does "mientras nadaba" show about the two tenses together?
study.product: Write a story (10–12 sentences) about a real or imagined trip using at least five preterite and five imperfect verbs, and include one interrupted action ("mientras… de repente…").

practice.q: Why does "mientras" usually take the imperfect?
practice.a: It describes an ongoing action in the background.

Using the imperfect for single completed events

items.q: Translate "Last summer we visited Mexico."

Explain why Spanish needs two past tenses.
items.answer: One marks completed events; the other sets the scene and describes ongoing or habitual actions.
